title: Sagana Patola: Characteristics
metaDescription: Sagana patola is a patola variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Sagana is a patola variety, also sold or known as Sagana sponge gourd. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Harbest Agribusiness (Seeds of Hope).

heroImage.alt: Ampalaya seedlings planted through plastic mulch on raised beds, the kind of farm where Sagana patola is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Sagana sponge gourd, this is the same patola. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [patola variety finder](/crop-varieties/patola), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: first harvest 45 to 58 days after sowing. No trial on record checks this figure yet, so treat it as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit patola fields most often: [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [melon fly](/pests/melon-fly), [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew), [squash beetle](/pests/squash-beetle). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 45 to 58 days after sowing.
**Fruit:** Pointed, ridged and green, about 250 g.

blocks.text: These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual patola on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Sagana patola

Patola comes ridged or smooth. Pick the one your market buys, and a variety that keeps setting fruit on the trellis for weeks. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Sagana sponge gourd the same as Sagana?
items.a: Yes. Sagana sponge gourd is another name for Sagana. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Sagana?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
